title: Axiom Configuration Schema
description: Source of truth for config/user/config.json. Every key's `default` is filled in at load time (SchemaValidation.applyDefaults), so config readers never need their own fallbacks. `title`/`description`/`minimum`/`maximum`/`enum` drive the generated settings UI; `x-settings: false` hides a key from it (edited elsewhere, or UI-owned state); `x-options` names a dynamic option list ("screens", "chatProviders" and "chatPresets", "colors" for the 16 base theme colors, "languages" from config/i18n, "cursorThemes" for installed cursor themes, "timezones" for the system's time zones, "edgeMenus" for the ids of EdgeMenus); `x-showIf` ({ sibling: value | [values] | { not: value } }) hides a field unless a sibling matches; a key starting with `/` is a dotted path from the config root instead ("/Workspaces.layout"). `x-enumLabels` ({ value: label }) shows labels instead of raw enum values in dropdowns. `x-multiline: true` edits a string in a growing text area. `x-categories` at the root lists the settings sidebar's categories in order, each `{ name, icon, page }` (`page`: a hand-built part after its cards, `views/settings/<page>.qml`); sections join one with `x-category`. `x-libraryGroups` at the root lists, in order, the groups the bar editor's and layouts editor's libraries sort their types into (by category); each bar widget and overlay module definition joins one with `x-libraryGroup`. `x-beside: true` on a field puts it beside the field before it on its settings card, each taking half the width. `x-order` on an object schema lists the keys its form shows first, in order (a schema reaches QML as a map, whose keys come out sorted). `x-defaultSize` ([w, h] in grid units, four to a card) on an overlay module definition is the size it's added at, and `x-minSize` the least a drop into a gap shrinks it to (half the default when left out); `x-icon` on a module or view definition is its Material Symbols icon name in the editor. `x-hosts` on a module definition lists where it may be placed ("overlay", "edgeMenu", "lockscreen", "greeter", "desktop"; the first two when left out, so the lock screen, the greeter and the desktop only take modules that list them). `x-greeter: true` on a Hyprland.managed option carries it to the greeter (its Hyprland takes the option in managed mode). A `$ref` may carry keys beside it (`default`, `title`, …), which override the definition's. `x-required: true` on one makes it part of every grid on its hosts: it can't be removed or duplicated, and the library doesn't offer it. `x-canvasDetail` names a module property the layouts editor shows on its tile (a list joined), and `x-canvasFill` a color property the tile is filled with. `x-takeover: true` marks a setting that takes something over on this PC (the Hyprland mode, the lock screen, idle, polkit, the greeter): loading a saved config, the defaults, an example or an import keeps its current value (ConfigExamples.keepTakeovers). Bar widgets are a oneOf discriminated by `type`, and get their `properties` defaults filled like everything else.

version.description: Config format version, used for automatic migration.

Lockscreen.title: Lockscreen
Lockscreen.description: Which locker locks the session. The Idle settings can lock after some idle time; an idle daemon of your own should lock through `qs -c axiom ipc call lockscreen lock` for the built-in or hyprlock modes.

mode.title: Locker
mode.description: Built-in uses the Wayland session-lock protocol with PAM, like hyprlock. hyprlock mode runs hyprlock with a config generated from the axiom theme. None leaves locking to your own locker.

lockCommand.title: Lock command
lockCommand.description: What axiom's lock buttons run when the locker is your own.

blurWallpaper.title: Blur wallpaper
blurWallpaper.description: Blur the wallpaper behind the lock screen.

layout.title: Built-in lock screen
layout.description: What the built-in locker shows, edited on the Layouts page: its modules on a grid of columns × rows units, fitted to each monitor.

Greeter.title: Login screen
Greeter.description: Axiom as your login screen (a greetd greeter), laid out on the Layouts page like the lock screen. It runs as greetd's own user from a copy of axiom installed for it, and shows what axiom exports for it here: no root is needed to change it once it's set up.

enabled.description: Set up as the login screen (set by its card's Install and Remove, never by hand).

source.title: Code from
source.description: Where Install and Update take the login screen's code. Git fetches it as root from the repository axiom was installed from, following releases or main as axiom's updates do: nothing that can write to your clone can change it. Local copies your clone as it is (the checked-out branch, uncommitted changes included), for working on axiom: any program running as you could change what the login screen runs before you next update it.

monitor.title: Login monitor
monitor.description: The monitor the login box shows on. The others show the layout without it, or only the background.

rememberUser.title: Remember the last user
rememberUser.description: Start on whoever logged in last, and on their last session. Off starts with an empty user field.

layout.title: Login screen
layout.description: What the login screen shows, edited on the Layouts page: its modules on a grid of columns × rows units, fitted to each monitor.

Idle.title: Idle
Idle.description: What happens when you step away: dimming, locking, turning the screens off and suspending, run by hypridle.

enabled.title: Manage hypridle
enabled.description: axiom runs hypridle with a config of its own (~/.local/state/axiom/hypridle.conf) and stops any other hypridle while this is on. Your own hypridle.conf is never touched; remove your own hypridle autostart line.

dimTimeout.title: Dim the screens after
dimTimeout.description: 0 never dims. Brightness comes back when you return.

dimMode.title: Dim

x-enumLabels.by: By a share of the current brightness

dimMode.description: A set brightness leaves screens already darker as they are. A share always dims, unless a screen is already at 0.

dimLevel.title: Dim to
dimLevel.description: Screens already darker stay as they are.

dimBy.title: Dim by
dimBy.description: How much of each screen's current brightness to take away: 50% takes 80% down to 40%.

lockTimeout.title: Lock after
lockTimeout.description: 0 never locks on idle. Locks with the Lockscreen settings' locker.

lockBeforeSleep.title: Lock before sleep
lockBeforeSleep.description: Lock the session before the computer suspends or hibernates.

screenOnAfterSleep.title: Screens on after sleep
screenOnAfterSleep.description: Turn the screens back on when the computer wakes.

respectInhibitors.title: Respect apps that keep the screen on
respectInhibitors.description: Video players and browsers can ask to stay awake over D-Bus and systemd. The caffeine widget works either way.

listeners.title: Extra listeners
listeners.description: Commands of your own to run after a time idle, and when you return.

Polkit.title: Authentication prompts
Polkit.description: The password prompt apps show when they need administrator rights (polkit): installing updates, mounting drives, changing system settings.

enabled.title: Use axiom's prompt
enabled.description: axiom becomes the session's polkit agent: the screen dims and the prompt opens in the middle of the focused monitor. A session has one agent, so axiom stops any other (hyprpolkitagent, KDE's, GNOME's) and leaves it out of the autostart; turned off, a stopped systemd agent starts again.

NightLight.title: Night light
NightLight.description: Warmer screen colors in the evening, through hyprsunset (or wlsunset). The Night light quick action, `/nightlight` in the launcher and `qs -c axiom ipc call nightLight toggle` switch it by hand; that lasts until the next scheduled change.

schedule.title: On a schedule
schedule.description: Turn the night light on and off at set times.

endAt.title: Turn off at
endAt.description: 24-hour time, like 07:00. Earlier than the start runs past midnight.

temperature.title: Color temperature
temperature.description: Lower is warmer. 6500 K is the screens' own color.

gamma.title: Gamma
gamma.description: Dims the screens a little further while the night light is on. 100% leaves them as they are.

language.title: Language
language.description: Language for the shell's text, dates and clock. Each file in config/i18n adds one.

displayName.title: Display name
displayName.description: Name shown on the lockscreen and in chat. Empty uses your login name.

primaryMonitor.title: Primary monitor
primaryMonitor.description: Monitor that hosts the lockscreen input, and the surfaces below when they're on one monitor. Empty uses the first screen.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where the overlay, launcher, power menu and OSD appear (each can override this). Focused monitor opens them on the one with your active workspace (and mouse); every monitor opens them on all of them at once. The workspace overview always opens on the monitor under the mouse.

Launcher.title: Launcher
Launcher.description: The search launcher: apps, open windows, a calculator, web search, running commands, and / commands that control the shell.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where the launcher opens. As in General follows General > Monitors; the primary monitor is the one set in General; the focused monitor is the one with your active workspace (and mouse); every monitor shows it on all of them at once.

edge.title: Screen edge
edge.description: Screen edge the launcher opens from, or is held off when detached.

position.title: Position along edge
position.description: Where along the edge its centre sits: 0 is the start (left/top), 100 the end. It never runs off the screen.

detached.title: Detach from edge
detached.description: A separate box floating off the edge. Off, the launcher grows out of the screen border or a solid bar, as popouts do, and runs straight off a bare screen edge.

distance.title: Distance from edge
distance.description: How far across the free screen it sits: 0 lines it up with a detached dock or OSD on that edge, 50 centres it.

reverse.title: Search bar at the bottom
reverse.description: Put the search field under the results, with the best match nearest to it. Suits the bottom edge.

maxResults.title: Results shown
maxResults.description: How many rows fit before the list scrolls.

showBackdrop.title: Dim background
showBackdrop.description: Dim the whole screen behind the launcher, under the bars and border.

backdrop.title: Backdrop darkness
backdrop.description: How dark the screen behind the launcher goes.

showDescriptions.title: Descriptions
showDescriptions.description: Show a second line under each result (an app's generic name, a window's class, a command's description).

showRecent.title: Frequent apps when empty
showRecent.description: List your most used apps before you type anything.

showHint.title: Controls hint
showHint.description: Show the search prefixes and keys under the results.

hiddenApps.title: Hidden apps
hiddenApps.description: Desktop entry ids never shown, comma-separated (e.g. avahi-discover, qv4l2).

windows.title: Open windows
windows.description: Also match open windows by title and class; picking one focuses it.

calculator.title: Calculator
calculator.description: Show the result of math as you type it (or after =), using qalc. Enter copies the result.

commands.title: Shell commands (/)
commands.description: Type / for commands that control the shell: themes, volume, wifi, bluetooth, overlay pages, session and more.

runCommands.title: Run commands (>)
runCommands.description: Type > and a command to run it. Shift+Enter runs it in the terminal.

webSearch.title: Web search (?)
webSearch.description: Offer a web search for what you typed, last in the list (or first after ?).

searchEngine.title: Search engine URL
searchEngine.description: {} is replaced by the search terms.

chat.title: Ask chat (@)
chat.description: Type @ and a question to ask it in the overlay's Chat module, with the default preset.

clipboard.title: Clipboard history (:)
clipboard.description: Type : (or /clipboard) to search what you've copied; Enter copies it again, Shift+Enter removes it. axiom keeps the history in memory only, never on disk, and skips anything a password manager marks as sensitive. Turn this off if you copy passwords from apps that don't; turning it off clears the history.

clipboardSource.title: Clipboard history source
clipboardSource.description: axiom records text clips itself. cliphist uses cliphist's history instead, images included, and records text and images into it while this is on (alongside any cliphist store you run yourself).

emoji.title: Emoji (;)
emoji.description: Type ; (or /emoji) to search emoji by name or keyword; Enter copies one. With wtype installed, Shift+Enter also types it into the focused window.

Apps.title: Apps
Apps.description: The apps axiom opens: by the Terminal, File manager and Browser keybinds, and the launcher's terminal apps and Shift+Enter commands.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.description: Terminal used for commands run with Shift+Enter, for terminal apps and by the Terminal keybind. It's started as: terminal -e command.

fileManager.title: File manager
fileManager.description: Command the File manager keybind runs. Empty opens your home folder in the system's default file manager.

browser.title: Browser
browser.description: Command the Browser keybind runs. Empty starts the system's default web browser.

PowerMenu.title: Power menu
PowerMenu.description: The power menu: lock, suspend, hibernate, log out, reboot and power off, opened by the power button, a keybind or `qs -c axiom ipc call powermenu toggle`.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where the power menu opens. As in General follows General > Monitors; the primary monitor is the one set in General; the focused monitor is the one with your active workspace (and mouse); every monitor shows it on all of them at once.

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: Which actions the menu shows, in order.

confirm.title: Confirm destructive actions
confirm.description: Log out, reboot and power off ask for a second click (or Enter) first.

tileSize.title: Tile size
tileSize.description: Width and height of each action's tile.

showHeader.title: Greeting and uptime
showHeader.description: Show a greeting and how long the computer has been up above the actions.

showHint.title: Controls hint
showHint.description: Show the keys under the actions.

showBackdrop.title: Dim background
showBackdrop.description: Dim the whole screen behind the power menu, under the bars and border.

backdrop.title: Backdrop darkness
backdrop.description: How dark the screen behind the power menu goes.

Battery.title: Battery
Battery.description: Low and critical battery levels, on laptops: the Battery widget takes its low and critical colors at them, and a notification says when the battery drops to one.

notify.title: Low battery notifications
notify.description: Send a notification when the battery becomes low, and again when it becomes critical.

Notifications.title: Notifications
Notifications.description: Where notification toasts appear, how long they stay, and what the history keeps. Toasts sit inside the work area, the space the bars and screen border leave free, so a gap is measured from whatever is at that edge: a bar, the border's stroke, or the bare screen edge.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where toasts appear. As in General follows General > Monitors; the primary monitor is the one set in General; the focused monitor is the one with your active workspace when the notification arrives; every monitor shows each toast on all of them, and closing one closes the rest.

position.title: Corner
position.description: Corner of the work area the toasts stack from. Bottom corners stack upwards.

evenGaps.title: Even gaps
evenGaps.description: Use one gap for both sides of the corner. Turn off to set each side on its own.

gap.title: Gap
gap.description: Space between the toasts and the edges of the work area.

gapTop.title: Top gap
gapTop.description: Space between the toasts and the top of the work area.

gapBottom.title: Bottom gap
gapBottom.description: Space between the toasts and the bottom of the work area.

gapLeft.title: Left gap
gapLeft.description: Space between the toasts and the left of the work area.

gapRight.title: Right gap
gapRight.description: Space between the toasts and the right of the work area.

timeout.title: Toast duration
timeout.description: How long a toast stays up. Hovering it pauses the countdown.

appTimeouts.title: Use app timeouts
appTimeouts.description: When an app asks for its own duration, or for its notification to stay until dismissed, use that instead of the duration above.

criticalStays.title: Critical toasts stay
criticalStays.description: Critical notifications stay up until you dismiss them.

maxToasts.title: Visible toasts
maxToasts.description: How many toasts stack up at once. A new one pushes out the oldest.

quietFullscreen.title: Quiet over fullscreen
quietFullscreen.description: Show no toasts on a monitor whose workspace has a fullscreen window. Critical ones still show, and everything still goes to the history.

clearOnFocus.title: Clear when the app is focused
clearOnFocus.description: Focusing an app's window removes its notifications from the history.

removeOnClick.title: Remove when clicked
removeOnClick.description: Clicking a notification, or one of its actions, removes it from the history.

closeRemoves.title: Closing a toast removes it
closeRemoves.description: Closing a toast (its close button or a swipe) also removes the notification from the history. Off, it only hides the toast.

maxEntries.title: History size
maxEntries.description: How many notifications the history keeps. The oldest go first.

maxAgeDays.title: Keep for
maxAgeDays.description: Remove notifications older than this many days. 0 keeps them until removed.

Hyprland.title: Hyprland
Hyprland.description: How axiom sets Hyprland up. Needs Hyprland 0.55+ with a Lua config.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Applies on Save. The status card says what the change will do.

requiredSettings.title: Required settings
requiredSettings.description: Lock restore after a shell restart, ignoring apps' requests to maximize themselves, and a workspace slide animation.

wallpaperDaemon.title: Start awww
wallpaperDaemon.description: Start awww-daemon for the wallpaper picker.

key.title: Key
key.description: Modifiers and key, joined by +: "SUPER + SHIFT + space".

argument.title: Argument
argument.description: Search text, page, edge menu or dock id, direction, workspace number, special workspace name, resize step ("50 0"), screenshot kind (region, window or screen), command, or a Hyprland dispatcher as Lua (hl.dsp.layout("swapsplit")).

call.title: Call
call.description: For actions that open and close something: whether the bind toggles it, only opens it or only closes it.

description.title: Description
description.description: Label on the Keybinds page; empty uses the action's name. The action picks the section unless you write "Section: Label".

look.title: Window look
look.description: Hyprland settings that make windows match axiom, in every mode. While on, they win over your own Hyprland config, and they come along when you share or import a config.

shape.title: Match axiom's shape
shape.description: Window corners and border width follow Look & Feel → Shape.

gaps.title: Set window gaps
gaps.description: Floating bars and detached surfaces set to Automatic keep these gaps too.

blur.title: Set Hyprland's blur
blur.description: Hyprland has one blur, for windows and axiom's translucent surfaces alike. Off, your own Hyprland config's applies.

windowBlur.title: Blur transparent windows
windowBlur.description: Off, only axiom's surfaces blur (Look & Feel → Translucency).

blurXray.title: See-through blur
blurXray.description: Floating windows blur only the wallpaper, not the windows under them. Cheaper.

blurSpecial.title: Blur behind special workspaces
blurSpecial.description: Expensive: redraws the blur on every frame.

opacity.title: Set window opacity
opacity.description: Off, your own Hyprland config's applies.

managed.title: Managed config
managed.description: Written into hyprland.lua. Anything else goes in ~/.config/hypr/user/*.lua.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: How windows tile. For strips (Hyprland's scrolling columns), see Workspaces.

preserveSplit.title: Keep split direction
preserveSplit.description: Dwindle keeps a split's direction when the window is resized or moved.

smartSplit.title: Split by cursor position
smartSplit.description: Dwindle splits towards the side of the window the cursor is on.

smartResizing.title: Resize by cursor position
smartResizing.description: Resizing moves the edge nearest the cursor.

splitRatio.title: Split ratio
splitRatio.description: The first window's share of a new split; 100 splits evenly.

snap.title: Snap floating windows
snap.description: Floating windows snap to each other and the screen edges.

animationPreset.title: Style
animationPreset.description: Follow axiom's motion uses Look & Feel → Motion's speed, and turns Hyprland's animations off with axiom's.

workspaceWraparound.title: Wrap workspace animations
workspaceWraparound.description: Going from the last workspace to the first slides forward, not back.

curves.title: Curves
curves.description: Named bezier curves for the custom animations.

points.title: Points
points.description: x1, y1, x2, y2, as in CSS cubic-bezier().

customAnimations.title: Animations
customAnimations.description: One entry per animation to change; a parent (windows) covers its children (windowsIn, windowsOut, windowsMove).

curve.title: Curve
curve.description: A curve's name from above, or default.

style.title: Style
style.description: Optional: popin 80%, slide, slidevert, slidefade 20%, fade, gnomed, loop, once.

kbVariant.title: Layout variant
kbVariant.description: XKB variants, one per layout (e.g. colemak).

floatSwitchOverrideFocus.title: Crossing tiled/floating

x-enumLabels.2: Moves focus, also floating to floating

floatSwitchOverrideFocus.description: What moving the cursor between tiled and floating windows does.

sensitivity.title: Pointer speed
sensitivity.description: -100 to 100; 0 leaves it as the device reports.

cursorTheme.title: Cursor theme
cursorTheme.description: An installed cursor theme. None leaves the cursor alone.

noWarps.title: Never move the cursor
noWarps.description: Hyprland won't move the cursor to a window it focuses.

backgroundThemed.title: Background in a theme color
backgroundThemed.description: What shows where there's no wallpaper.

focusOnActivate.title: Focus windows that ask for it
focusOnActivate.description: e.g. a browser window opened from a link.

swallow.title: Terminals swallow what they open
swallow.description: A GUI app started from a terminal takes the terminal's place until it closes.

swallowRegex.title: Swallowing terminals
swallowRegex.description: A regex of terminal window classes.

workspaceBackAndForth.title: Workspace back and forth
workspaceBackAndForth.description: Going to the current workspace goes back to the previous one.

scrollEventDelay.title: Scroll bind delay
scrollEventDelay.description: How long a bound scroll ignores further scrolling.

xwaylandZeroScaling.title: Unscaled X11 apps
xwaylandZeroScaling.description: X11 apps draw at native resolution on scaled monitors, instead of blurry.

recommendedEnv.title: Recommended environment
recommendedEnv.description: The variables Hyprland's wiki recommends: GTK, Qt, Clutter and Electron apps run on Wayland (falling back to X11 where they can), Qt scales by pixel density and leaves window decorations to Hyprland. Your own below win over them.

env.title: Environment
env.description: Variables set before anything starts. Changes apply to apps started afterwards.

autostart.title: Autostart
autostart.description: Commands run once when Hyprland starts, after axiom.

theme.description: Active theme (set on the overlay's Themes page).

wallpaper.description: The primary monitor's wallpaper file URL, used by the lockscreen (set on the overlay's Themes page).

wallpapers.description: Monitor name → wallpaper file URL (set on the overlay's Themes page). A monitor with no entry shows `wallpaper`.

wallpaperBackend.title: Wallpaper backend
wallpaperBackend.description: What draws the wallpaper. Axiom needs nothing installed and crossfades; awww (AUR) adds wipe and wave transitions.

wallpaperFolder.title: Wallpaper folder
wallpaperFolder.description: Folder the wallpaper pickers list images from (jpg, png, bmp). A leading ~ is your home folder.

wallpaperMode.title: Wallpaper mode

x-enumLabels.variant: One for light, one for dark

wallpaperMode.description: Fixed keeps the wallpaper you pick. Rotate changes it on a timer, from the wallpaper folder. One for light, one for dark shows the wallpaper you picked for the theme's current variant on every monitor. A generated theme follows the wallpaper as it changes. Also set on the overlay's Themes page.

interval.title: Change every
interval.description: How long each wallpaper stays up.

order.title: Order
order.description: Random never picks the wallpaper already showing.

sameOnAll.title: Same on every monitor
sameOnAll.description: Show one wallpaper on all monitors. Off, each monitor gets its own.

variantWallpapers.description: The wallpapers for the light and dark variants, as file URLs (set on the overlay's Themes page).

enabled.title: Switch by time of day
enabled.description: Use the theme's light variant during the day and its dark one at night. Switching by hand lasts until the next change.

size.title: Size
size.description: Base font size (px). Larger text is derived from it.

radius.title: Corner radius
radius.description: Roundness of outer edges: the screen border, bars, popouts and windows (px). Everything inside follows it unless Panels & controls sets its own.

screenBorder.title: Screen border
screenBorder.description: Draw a frame around the screen edges.

screenMargin.title: Screen margin
screenMargin.description: Width of the screen frame, and the gap kept from the screen edges (px).

opacity.title: Surface opacity
opacity.description: How solid the shell's surfaces are: bars, the screen border, popouts, menus and panels. 100 is fully solid.

blur.title: Blur behind surfaces
blur.description: Hyprland blurs what shows through a translucent surface, with its own blur (Hyprland → Window look → Blur). It costs GPU time whenever what's behind or on a surface changes, more with a stronger blur and with windows blurred behind.

throughWindows.title: Blur windows behind surfaces
throughWindows.description: Off, bars, the border and popouts blur the wallpaper alone, which is cheaper. Tooltips and menus always blur what's behind them.

blurBackdrops.title: Blur backdrops
blurBackdrops.description: Also blur the whole screen behind the overlay, launcher, power menu and workspace overview. Costs more while they open.

pauseFullscreen.title: Pause blur over fullscreen apps
pauseFullscreen.description: While a fullscreen window (a game, a video) is open, nothing blurs, so a volume popup or notification over it costs nothing extra. Surfaces stay translucent.

enabled.title: Animations
enabled.description: Turn every animation in the shell on or off.

speed.title: Animation speed
speed.description: Speed of every animation. 100 is normal, 200 is twice as fast, 50 is half speed.

Widget.title: Panels & controls
Widget.description: Sizing for the overlay, popouts, launcher and settings. Each bar has its own, in the bar editor.

height.title: Control height
height.description: Height of buttons, fields and other controls (px).

padding.title: Padding
padding.description: Inner padding of panels, cards and controls (px).

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.description: Gap between items inside panels, cards and controls (px).

overrideRadius.title: Own corner radius
overrideRadius.description: Off: follows the corner radius in Look & Feel.

radius.title: Interior corner radius
radius.description: Roundness of what sits inside panels, cards and bars: buttons, fields, rows, cells and bar widgets. Outer edges (screen border, bars, popouts, the overlay's outer box) keep the main radius.

BarStyle.title: Bar style
BarStyle.description: How every bar draws its widgets, accents and shadow. A bar can take its own of any of these in the bar editor.

widgetStyle.title: Widget style
widgetStyle.description: How each widget shows its color: as its background, a faint tint, an outline, a line beside it, or on its icon. Plain text draws them straight onto the bar.

widgetShape.title: Shape
widgetShape.description: Rounded follows the widget corner radius. Slanted and arrow widgets take a little more room for their points.

widgetGrouping.title: Grouping
widgetGrouping.description: Merged: neighbouring widgets share one background. Powerline: each widget's shape runs into the next.

widgetEnds.title: Ends
widgetEnds.description: The ends of a slanted or arrow widget, or of a run of them: as shaped, rounded, or (arrows) pointed at both.

groupColor.title: Merged background
groupColor.description: Widget colors show on their icons instead.

widgetTextColor.title: Text color
widgetTextColor.description: One color for every widget's text and icons. Auto: each widget's own on a filled background, its color when tinted or outlined, else one that contrasts with the bar.

separatorStyle.title: Separators
separatorStyle.description: Drawn in the gap between neighbouring widgets in a section (not in a powerline). Give them room with Spacing.

accentLine.title: Accent line
accentLine.description: A line along the bar's edge toward the windows (inner) or the screen edge (outer); on pills, along each pill.

accentLineFade.title: Fade to
accentLineFade.description: Runs the line from its color into this one along the bar.

shadow.title: Shadow
shadow.description: Cast by every bar (or its pills) and by the screen border, inward all the way round. A transparent bar has nothing to cast one; a solid bar on the border leaves it to the border.

shadowColor.title: Shadow color
shadowColor.description: Auto: black for a shadow, the accent for a glow.

Popouts.title: Popouts
Popouts.description: Behaviour shared by bar popouts and screen-edge popouts (side panel, OSD).

openDelay.title: Open delay
openDelay.description: How long to hover a bar widget or screen edge before its popout opens.

dismissDelay.title: Dismiss delay
dismissDelay.description: How long after the mouse leaves a popout before it closes.

edgeTriggerSize.title: Edge trigger size
edgeTriggerSize.description: Thickness of the hover strip at the screen edge that opens edge popouts.

padding.title: Padding
padding.description: Space between a popout's box and its content: bar popouts, OSDs, and edge menus that don't set their own.

Chat.title: Chat
Chat.description: The Chat overlay module, and the launcher's @ prefix. API keys are never stored here: set them on the card above (they go to your keyring, or $XDG_STATE_HOME/axiom/secrets.json without one), or in each provider's environment variable.

defaultProvider.title: Default provider
defaultProvider.description: Used by presets that don't name a provider of their own.

defaultPreset.title: Default preset
defaultPreset.description: What a new conversation starts with.

maxTokens.title: Longest reply
maxTokens.description: A reply that reaches this is cut off, with a note saying so.

keepConversations.title: Conversations kept
keepConversations.description: Older ones are deleted. 0 keeps none: conversations last until the shell restarts.

showThinking.title: Show thinking
showThinking.description: Ask models that reason for a summary of it, shown folded above the reply.

renderMarkdown.title: Format replies
renderMarkdown.description: Draw Markdown (headings, lists, tables, code blocks) instead of the raw text.

providers.title: Providers
providers.description: Where chats are sent. The OpenAI kind also covers Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, OpenRouter, Groq and anything else with an OpenAI-style API: set its address.

id.title: ID
id.description: Names the provider's key in the keyring and presets' provider field. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

baseUrl.title: Address
baseUrl.description: The API's base URL, up to and including its version (e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1).

keyEnv.title: Key variable
keyEnv.description: An environment variable that holds the key, if you keep it there. It wins over a stored key.

models.title: Models
models.description: Model ids to choose from, comma-separated. Fetch models on the card above fills this in.

defaultModel.title: Default model
defaultModel.description: Empty uses the first of the models.

fallbacks.title: Refusal fallback
fallbacks.description: When the model declines a request, the API retries it on another model within the same reply.

presets.title: Presets
presets.description: Saved setups to start a conversation with: a system prompt, and optionally a provider, model and effort of their own.

default.name: Default
default.systemPrompt: You are a helpful assistant built into the user's Linux desktop. Answer concisely, and use Markdown when it helps.

default.name: Coder
default.systemPrompt: You are an expert programmer. Lead with working code, then explain briefly. Prefer small, idiomatic changes.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: A provider ID. Empty uses the default provider.

model.title: Model
model.description: Empty uses the provider's default model.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: How hard a reasoning model thinks. Models that don't reason ignore it.

Notes.title: Notes
Notes.description: Where the Notes module keeps its notes: plain Markdown files, one per note, in folders of your own. Checklists are Markdown tasks (- [ ] item), so other Markdown editors read them too.

directory.title: Notes folder
directory.description: An absolute path (~/ works), e.g. a synced folder or a Markdown vault. Empty keeps notes in axiom's config/state/notes, which is not backed up.

extensions.title: File types
extensions.description: File extensions the note list shows, comma-separated. New notes are .md.

showHidden.title: Show hidden files
showHidden.description: List files and folders whose names start with a dot.

confirmDelete.title: Confirm before deleting
confirmDelete.description: Deleted notes and folders go to the trash. Without gio (glib2) deleting is permanent, and always asks first.

Calendar.title: Calendar
Calendar.description: Events from CalDAV accounts (iCloud, Fastmail, Nextcloud, …) and .ics subscriptions, for the calendar popout, the Calendar, Clock & calendar and Agenda modules, the Next event bar widget and the Calendar page. Passwords are never stored here: they go to your keyring (or $XDG_STATE_HOME/axiom/secrets.json without one).

defaultCalendar.title: New events go to
defaultCalendar.description: The calendar picked for a new event (the launcher's /event uses it too).

defaultDuration.title: Event length
defaultDuration.description: How long a new event lasts until you change it.

defaultReminder.title: Reminder
defaultReminder.description: How long before a new event's start its reminder fires. -1 adds none.

reminders.title: Notify reminders
reminders.description: Show a notification when an event's reminder is due (while axiom runs).

syncInterval.title: Sync every
syncInterval.description: How often calendars are checked for changes, while something shows them or reminders are on.

pastMonths.title: Months back
pastMonths.description: How far back events are kept. Paging past it fetches more.

use24Hour.title: 24-hour times
use24Hour.description: How event times show everywhere events do.

maxDots.title: Dots per day
maxDots.description: Most calendar-colored dots under a day in the month grids.

showOnLockscreen.title: Events on the lock screen
showOnLockscreen.description: The Clock & calendar module shows the day's events on the lock screen too (read-only). Anyone at the locked screen can read them.

Weather.title: Weather
Weather.description: Where and how every weather widget and module gets its weather, from Open-Meteo (no account needed).

location.title: Location
location.description: City name to look up. Empty uses your IP's location.

latitude.title: Latitude
latitude.description: Exact coordinates; with longitude, overrides the location lookup.

OSD.title: OSD
OSD.description: On-screen displays of volume, microphone and brightness bars, shown when one of their bars changes.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Show the OSDs when one of their bars changes.

scrollToChange.title: Scroll to change
scrollToChange.description: Scrolling over a bar raises or lowers its level.

scrollStep.title: Scroll step
scrollStep.description: How much one wheel notch changes the level.

osds.title: OSDs
osds.description: Each OSD has its own place and bars. A change opens every OSD holding that bar.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Show the docks below. Off hides every dock.

docks.title: Docks
docks.description: Each dock has its own place, apps and behaviour.

ThemeIntegrations.title: Theme integrations
ThemeIntegrations.description: Re-theme external apps whenever the shell theme changes. Each writes its own axiom file; turned on, it shows the line that loads that file from the app's config, to copy or to apply (which backs your config up first).

gtk.title: GTK
gtk.description: Writes axiom.css beside GTK 3 and GTK 4's gtk.css, and follows light/dark. GTK3 apps need the adw-gtk3 theme (pacman -S adw-gtk-theme).

qt.title: Qt (qt5ct / qt6ct)
qt.description: Writes an "axiom" color scheme for qt5ct and qt6ct (Qt apps need QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt5ct / qt6ct).

kitty.title: Kitty
kitty.description: Writes kitty/axiom.conf. Reloads kitty when allow_remote_control is on.

alacritty.title: Alacritty
alacritty.description: Writes alacritty/axiom.toml. Alacritty reloads it by itself.
alacritty.x-hookupNote: Alacritty loads imported files before its own, so colors set in alacritty.toml still win: remove them to use axiom's.

foot.title: Foot
foot.description: Writes foot/axiom.ini. Applies to new windows.

wezterm.title: WezTerm
wezterm.description: Writes the "axiom" color scheme. WezTerm picks it up on its next config reload.

x-hookup.where: In wezterm.lua, before the final 'return config'.

ghostty.title: Ghostty
ghostty.description: Writes the "axiom" theme. Ghostty 1.2+ reloads it.

nvim.title: Neovim
nvim.description: Writes the theme for the axiom_theme module, and reloads running instances.
nvim.x-hookupNote: Neovim has no single line to add. Its colors come from colorscheme plugins your config loads, often lazily through a plugin manager and after init.lua has run, so a file read at startup would be overridden. axiom writes the theme to $XDG_STATE_HOME/axiom/nvim-theme.json; the axiom_theme module reads it, picks a colorscheme you map to it (or builds one from the palette) and reloads when the theme changes. Copy the module into your config, then call its setup() once your plugins are loaded.

x-hookup.where: In init.lua, after your plugin manager's setup (with lazy.nvim, after require("lazy").setup(…)).

helix.title: Helix
helix.description: Writes the "axiom" theme. Helix 23.10+ reloads it.

vscode.title: VS Code / VSCodium
vscode.description: Installs a local "Axiom" color theme extension.

x-hookup.where: In settings.json (Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)), or pick Axiom under Preferences: Color Theme.

zed.title: Zed
zed.description: Writes the "Axiom" theme, which follows light/dark. Zed reloads it.

x-hookup.where: In Zed's settings.json (zed: open settings), or pick Axiom in the theme selector (ctrl-k ctrl-t). With "mode": "system", set both "light" and "dark" to Axiom.

vesktop.title: Vesktop / Vencord
vesktop.description: Writes the axiom.theme.css Vencord theme for Vesktop (and Vencord, Equibop, Equicord). Discord re-colors live.

x-hookup.where: In Vesktop: Settings → Vencord → Themes, switch it on.

firefox.title: Firefox / LibreWolf / Zen
firefox.description: Writes chrome/axiom.css into every profile of Firefox and its forks (LibreWolf, Zen, Floorp, Waterfox; Flatpak too), recoloring the browser's tabs, toolbars, menus and sidebar. Applies from each browser's next start; websites only follow light/dark.
firefox.x-hookupNote: Apply sets up every profile it finds: it imports axiom.css at the top of each profile's chrome/userChrome.css, and turns on toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets in its user.js, which Firefox needs before it reads userChrome.css. Restart the browser afterwards.

k9s.title: k9s
k9s.description: Writes the "axiom" skin. k9s reloads it by itself.

x-hookup.where: In ~/.config/k9s/config.yaml, merged into its k9s: section.

cava.title: Cava
cava.description: Writes cava/colors/axiom.conf (and a Cava config including it, when there is none). Reloads running Cava.

btop.title: btop
btop.description: Writes the "axiom" theme. Applies from btop's next start.

ncspot.title: ncspot
ncspot.description: Writes the colors into the [theme] table of ncspot's config.toml, between axiom's markers. Reloads running ncspot.
ncspot.x-hookupNote: ncspot can't load a separate theme file, so unlike the other integrations this one edits your config.toml: Apply adds two marker lines to its [theme] table, and every theme change rewrites the lines between them. Keep your own edits outside the markers. A key you set in [theme] yourself wins over axiom's.

x-hookup.text:
# axiom theme: begin (rewritten on every theme change)
# axiom theme: end

lazygit.title: lazygit
lazygit.description: Writes lazygit/axiom.yml. Applies from lazygit's next start.
lazygit.x-hookupNote: This sets LG_CONFIG_FILE, which takes the place of any value you set yourself: add your own files to it.

bat.title: bat / delta
bat.description: Writes the "axiom" syntax theme for bat and delta, and rebuilds bat's cache.

zathura.title: zathura
zathura.description: Writes zathura/axiom: the interface, search highlights and recolor mode's page colors. Reloads running zathura.

overrides.description: App name → icon path/URL, for apps whose tray or window icon doesn't resolve.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where the overlay opens. As in General follows General > Monitors; the primary monitor is the one set in General; the focused monitor is the one with your active workspace (and mouse); every monitor shows it on all of them at once.

size.title: Overlay size
size.description: Size of the overlay's cards, relative to what fits the screen. Pages that would still overflow are shrunk to fit.

closeOnEscape.title: Close on Escape
closeOnEscape.description: Close the overlay when Escape is pressed (unless something in it, like a popup, uses the key first).

closeOnOutsideClick.title: Close on outside click
closeOnOutsideClick.description: Close the overlay when you click outside it: on a bar, the screen border or another monitor.

views.description: Pages shown in the overlay, in order: your Custom pages, each a grid of modules, and the tool pages (shown as icons after them).

Workspaces.title: Workspaces
Workspaces.description: How workspaces are laid out, for the bar's workspace widget, the workspace overview and the Workspaces module. Point your workspace keybinds at `qs -c axiom ipc call workspaces <left|right|up|down|go N|nth N>` (and the move… versions) so they follow it too.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: Standard: workspaces 1 to N, shared by every monitor. Per monitor: each monitor has its own 1 to N workspaces. Grid: each monitor has its own columns × rows workspaces. Per monitor and grid assign monitors a stable order (the primary monitor first, then the rest by their monitor identity), so a hotplug or Hyprland restart can't reshuffle which monitor owns which ids.

wrap.title: Wrap around
wrap.description: Stepping past the last workspace (of a row or column in a grid) goes back to the first.

animate.title: Directional slides
animate.description: Slide between workspaces whatever Hyprland's own workspace animation style is: sideways in the standard layout; in a grid, sideways between columns and vertically between rows, going by row first, then column.

strips.title: Strips
strips.description: Monitors whose windows sit side by side on a strip that scrolls (Hyprland's scrolling layout) instead of tiling. New windows open as a new column after the focused one.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Empty uses the primary monitor; All monitors makes every monitor a strip, unless another entry names it.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Horizontal: columns side by side, scrolling sideways. Vertical: rows one under another, scrolling up and down.

stripColumnWidth.title: Column width
stripColumnWidth.description: A new column's share of the monitor.

WorkspaceOverlay.title: Workspace overview
WorkspaceOverlay.description: The full-screen workspace board (laid out as in Workspaces): drag windows between workspaces, right-drag to resize, middle-click to close.

background.title: Workspace background
background.description: What each workspace shows behind its windows.

dimInactive.title: Dim other workspaces
dimInactive.description: How much darker workspaces other than the active one are drawn.

size.title: Size
size.description: How much of the screen the grid may take.

backdrop.title: Backdrop darkness
backdrop.description: How dark the screen behind the grid goes.

showNumbers.title: Workspace numbers
showNumbers.description: Show each workspace's number in its corner.

showTitles.title: Window titles
showTitles.description: Show a window's title while it's hovered.

showHint.title: Controls hint
showHint.description: Show the mouse controls under the grid.

WindowSwitcher.title: Window switcher
WindowSwitcher.description: Your windows, most recently used first, while the switch windows keys are held (ALT + Tab and ALT + SHIFT + Tab on the Keybinds page). Releasing the modifier focuses the chosen window; Escape keeps the current one.

previews.title: Window previews
previews.description: Show each window's live contents; off shows app icons.

showDelay.title: Show after
showDelay.description: How long the keys must be held before the switcher shows. A quicker tap swaps to the last window without showing it.

SelfUpdate.title: axiom updates
SelfUpdate.description: Updates come from the repository axiom was cloned from: its release tags, or its main branch. An update only fast-forwards: a clone with changed files or commits of its own is never touched.

channel.title: Follow
channel.description: Releases updates to each new release tag. Main branch updates to every new commit on main: newer, but less tested.

mode.title: Updates
mode.description: Checked when the shell starts and once a day. Update automatically installs an update and notifies you; Notify me sends a notification that opens this page. Off never checks.

Bars.description: Bars, edited in the overlay's bar editor.

EdgeMenus.description: Menus that pop out of a screen edge, filled with overlay modules, edited on the overlay's Layouts page. Opened by a bar Button (Edge menu action), their edge trigger, or `qs -c axiom ipc call edgeMenu toggle <id>`.

Desktop.description: Overlay modules on the desktop, under the windows, edited on the overlay's Layouts page. Each monitor shows its own layout if it has one, else the primary monitor's (on the primary monitor), else the one for all monitors; each is fitted inside the bars and the border.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Layouts of monitors by name (their connector), ahead of the primary monitor's and the one for all.

DesktopLayout.description: A desktop's overlay modules on a bounded grid of columns × rows units, fitted to each monitor inside its bars and border (Desktop).

enabled.description: Shown. Off on a monitor's own layout leaves that monitor's desktop empty.

monitor.description: The monitor (connector name) a layout in Desktop.monitors is for.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: Grid units across. The grid is stretched to fill the room inside the bars and border, so match its shape.

fineGrid.title: Double grid
fineGrid.description: Split each grid unit in two each way, for finer placement. Modules keep their size and spot.

moduleBorders.title: Module borders
moduleBorders.description: Draw each module's card box, frosted over the wallpaper while the shell blurs. Off shows modules straight on the wallpaper.

ScreenLayout.description: A screen of overlay modules on a bounded grid of columns × rows units, fitted to each monitor: the built-in lock screen (Lockscreen.layout) and the greeter (Greeter.layout).

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: Grid units across. The grid is stretched to fill each monitor, so match your screen's shape (16 × 9 for 16:9).

fineGrid.title: Double grid
fineGrid.description: Split each grid unit in two each way, for finer placement. Modules keep their size and spot.

otherScreens.title: Other monitors

x-enumLabels.layout: The same modules, without the password

otherScreens.description: What monitors other than the one with the password field show.

background.title: Background
background.description: Each monitor's wallpaper (blurred when Blur wallpaper is on), or a plain color.

dim.title: Dim
dim.description: Darken the background so the modules stand out.

moduleBorders.title: Module borders
moduleBorders.description: Draw each module's card box. Off shows modules straight on the background. The password field and the greeting have their own switches.

passwordBorder.title: Password field border
passwordBorder.description: Draw a card box around the password field.

greetingBorder.title: Greeting border
greetingBorder.description: Draw a card box around the greeting.

name.title: Name
name.description: Shown on its tab here. Empty names it by its edge.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where the dock appears. As in General follows General > Monitors; the primary monitor is the one set in General; the focused monitor is the one with your active workspace (and mouse), and the dock moves with it; every monitor shows it on all of them at once; a specific monitor is the one picked below.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Monitor the dock is shown on. Empty uses the primary monitor.

position.title: Position along edge
position.description: Where along the edge its centre sits: 0 is the start (left/top), 100 the end. It never runs off the screen.

detached.title: Detach from edge
detached.description: A separate box held off the edge. Off, the dock grows out of the screen border or a solid bar, as popouts do, and runs straight off a bare screen edge.

gap.title: Gap
gap.description: Space between the dock and the border or bar on its edge, and at the ends. Auto lines it up with a floating bar on its edge, else with your windows. Reserving its space, it keeps Hyprland's gap between windows from them.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: Always shown stays up. Show on hover slides in when the pointer rests on the screen edge. Hide when a window overlaps stays up until a window on the monitor's workspace covers it, then works like Show on hover.

reserveSpace.title: Reserve space
reserveSpace.description: Keep windows out of the dock's strip, as a bar does. Magnified icons still grow over windows.

openDelay.title: Open delay
openDelay.description: How long the pointer rests on the edge before the dock slides in.

closeDelay.title: Close delay
closeDelay.description: How long after the pointer leaves the dock it slides away.

triggerSize.title: Trigger size
triggerSize.description: How far in from the screen edge the hover strip reaches.

padding.title: Padding
padding.description: Space between the dock's box and its icons.

magnify.title: Magnify under the pointer
magnify.description: Grow the icons near the pointer, as macOS does.

magnifiedSize.title: Magnified size
magnifiedSize.description: Size of the icon right under the pointer.

magnifyRange.title: Magnify range
magnifyRange.description: How many icons to each side of the pointer grow with it.

showRunning.title: Show running apps
showRunning.description: Also show apps with open windows that aren't pinned, after the pinned ones.

windowScope.title: Windows counted
windowScope.description: Which windows make an app running here: its indicator, what a click focuses, and the running apps shown.

separator.title: Separator
separator.description: A line between the pinned apps and the other running ones.

showLabels.title: Names on hover
showLabels.description: Show an app's name in a tooltip when the pointer rests on it.

name.title: Name
name.description: Shown on its tab here. Empty names it by its bars.

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.description: Where the OSD appears. As in General follows General > Monitors; the primary monitor is the one set in General; the focused monitor is the one with your active workspace (and mouse); every monitor shows it on all of them at once; a specific monitor is the one picked below.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Monitor the OSD is shown on. Empty uses the primary monitor.

edge.title: Screen edge
edge.description: Screen edge the OSD slides out of.

position.title: Position along edge
position.description: Where along the edge it opens: 0 is the start (left/top), 100 the end.

detached.title: Detach from edge
detached.description: A separate box held off the edge. Off, the OSD grows out of the screen border or a solid bar, as popouts do, and runs straight off a bare screen edge.

gap.title: Gap
gap.description: Space between the OSD and the border or bar on its edge, and at the ends. Auto lines it up with a floating bar on its edge, else with your windows.

orientation.title: Bar orientation
orientation.description: Vertical bars sit side by side; horizontal bars stack as rows.

alongEdge.title: Line up along the edge
alongEdge.description: Put the bars end to end in one line along the edge, instead of stacked away from it: the OSD is longer but sticks out less. Shown only while the bars run along the edge.

openOnHover.title: Open on hover
openOnHover.description: Also open the OSD when the mouse touches the screen edge where it appears.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the OSD stays open after the last change.

showPercent.title: Show percentages
showPercent.description: Show each bar's level as a percentage beside its icon.

bars.title: Bars
bars.description: One bar per entry, in order. System volume is the output device's volume, Other apps is the first playing stream no App bar (in any OSD) matches, Microphone is the input device's volume, and Brightness is the monitor's own (a laptop panel through brightnessctl, an external monitor over DDC/CI through ddcutil; left out on a monitor that has neither).

apps.title: Apps
apps.description: Comma-separated; each matched as a substring of a stream's binary or name. The bar shows the first listed app with a stream open, and a change sets every matching stream.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: Icon shown on the bar: a Material Symbols name (fonts.google.com/icons), or text. Empty follows the level for system volume, microphone and brightness.

allMonitors.title: All monitors
allMonitors.description: The bar sets every monitor with a brightness control at once, instead of only the one the OSD is on.

showOsd.title: Opens the OSD
showOsd.description: A change on this bar opens the OSD (it always keeps an open one open).

id.title: Id
id.description: What bar buttons, keybinds and IPC calls open this menu by. Set when the menu is made.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Monitor this menu is shown on. Empty uses the primary monitor.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Floating opens over your windows. Integrated opens outside the screen border and bars, pushing them and your windows inwards.

offset.description: Cells of its lattice the menu sits from centred along its edge, positive towards the end (right or down), kept on the screen. Set by the arrows on the layouts editor's grid.

gridOffset.description: Shifts the lattice the menu's modules sit on along its edge (centred on the screen) by this many px, positive towards the end. Set beside the arrows on the layouts editor's grid.

length.title: Length
length.description: Whole edge stretches the menu along its edge, sharing the room evenly between its rows (or columns on a top or bottom edge).

moduleScale.title: Module size
moduleScale.description: Size of the menu's modules, relative to the overlay's cards on its monitor (which follow Overlay size).

fineGrid.title: Double grid
fineGrid.description: Split each grid unit in two each way, for finer placement. Modules keep their size and spot.

detached.title: Detach from edge
detached.description: A separate box held off the edge, instead of growing out of it.

gap.title: Gap
gap.description: Space between the menu and the border or bar on its edge, and at its ends. Auto lines it up with a floating bar on its edge, else with your windows.

frame.title: Frame
frame.description: Draw a rounded box along the whole edge, with the modules inside it, lined up with the screen border.

padding.title: Padding
padding.description: Space between the menu's box and its modules. Auto uses the Popouts padding.

moduleBorders.title: Module borders
moduleBorders.description: Draw each module's card box. Turn off to show modules straight on the menu's background, e.g. a menu with a single module.

pinButton.title: Pin button
pinButton.description: Show a pin in the menu's corner. A pinned menu stays open until you unpin it.

openOnHover.title: Open on hover
openOnHover.description: Open when the pointer rests on the screen edge.

openDelay.title: Open delay
openDelay.description: How long the pointer rests on the edge before the menu opens.

triggerSize.title: Trigger size
triggerSize.description: How far in from the screen edge the hover strip reaches.

triggerLength.title: Trigger length
triggerLength.description: Length of the hover strip along the edge, centred on the menu. Auto matches the menu's own length.

closeOnLeave.title: Close when the pointer leaves
closeOnLeave.description: Close shortly after the pointer leaves the menu. A pinned menu stays open.

closeDelay.title: Close delay
closeDelay.description: How long after the pointer leaves the menu closes.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Placed on a grid of quarter cards, like a Custom overlay page's.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Monitor this bar is shown on. Empty uses the primary monitor; All monitors puts an identical copy on each.

widgetSize.title: Widget size
widgetSize.description: How thick the widgets are across the bar. The bar grows to fit them, their padding, and any border it shares an edge with.

padding.title: Padding
padding.description: Space between the widgets and the bar's visible edges, on both sides.

background.title: Background
background.description: Every bar but a solid one sits inside the screen border. Pills grow out of it; floating bars and pills are held away from it.

floatGap.title: Float gap
floatGap.description: How far a floating bar keeps from the screen border (or the screen edge), across the bar and at its ends. Auto keeps Hyprland's gap to the screen edges, as your windows do. Windows always keep Hyprland's gap between windows from the bar.

pillPadding.title: Pill padding
pillPadding.description: Extra space around a pill's widgets (px). They sit the screen margin plus this from the screen edge, and as far from the pill's other edges.

pillMerge.title: Merge distance
pillMerge.description: Groups closer than this share one pill (px).

lockCenter.title: Lock center
lockCenter.description: Keep the center section dead center on the bar. The other sections shrink or hide widgets on their own side instead of pushing it.

reserveSpace.title: Reserve space
reserveSpace.description: Keep windows from tiling underneath the bar.

widgetPadding.title: Widget padding
widgetPadding.description: Space inside each widget, before its icon or text.

widgetSpacing.title: Inner spacing
widgetSpacing.description: Gap between items inside a widget.

overrideFontSize.title: Own font size
overrideFontSize.description: Off: the bar follows the font size in Look & Feel.

overrideRadius.title: Own corner radius
overrideRadius.description: Off: widgets follow the interior corner radius in Panels & controls. Pills follow the corner radius in Look & Feel.

overrideWidgetStyle.title: Own widget style
overrideWidgetStyle.description: Off: the bar follows the Bar style settings in Look & Feel.

widgetStyle.title: Widget style
widgetStyle.description: How each widget shows its color: as its background, a faint tint, an outline, a line beside it, or on its icon. Plain text draws them straight onto the bar.

widgetShape.title: Shape
widgetShape.description: Rounded follows the widget corner radius. Slanted and arrow widgets take a little more room for their points.

widgetGrouping.title: Grouping
widgetGrouping.description: Merged: neighbouring widgets share one background. Powerline: each widget's shape runs into the next.

widgetEnds.title: Ends
